sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. sources.title: Has Rockstar taken the "Grand Theft Auto" out of GTA 6? Or has it just gamified car-jacking properly for the first time?
sources.text: It's impossible to have a big game launch these days without some section of the internet, somewhere, finding grievances with the final product because it does not align with the expectations they had pre-release. The most recent upset comes in the form of Grand Theft Auto 6 's revised take on, well, grand theft auto. In case you're one of the few still unfamiliar, grand theft auto is more than the titular moniker for Rockstar's premier crime simulation series; it's actually a US legal term for the act of stealing or attempting to steal a motor vehicle. In most previous GTA entries, this was a central part of the core gameplay loop: accept a mission, nick a car, complete the mission, nick another car, getaway. It's an endemic part of the loop, and has become so popular and identifiable as such that even other games - Watch Dogs , Saint's Row, Cyberpunk 2077 , and so on - have emulated the mechanic. So it makes sense that the internet is in a bit of a spin about GTA 6's more mature and restrained take on its eponymous crime. A quick, no-frills getaway in a vehicle you've hijacked on the road isn't always the most effective option. A mindless crime spree on the streets of Leonida is not a simple thing to pull off, nor an easy thing to live down. In this game, actions have consequences, and an ill-timed or ill-judged car jacking can quickly and efficiently put an end to your criminal ambitions. That's not to say you cannot simply steal cars. Of course you can: the option to saunter up to an occupied vehicle and jack it from its registered owner is available to you from the very beginning of the game. But the citizens of Leonida aren't going to take your wanton act of foolishness lying down; many of the motorists in the county will fight back, pull a piece on you, or run you over mid-robbery attempt. Even if you are lucky to find one of the more pliant residents of the city, you might find something peculiar is happening in their car. I jacked a woman in the city over the weekend, and the cat she was ferrying from place to place decided to attack me, causing me to crash. I've heard other people say they've had muffled cries coming from the boot of the car where someone is transporting a hostage, or incidents where they've jacked the same person multiple times, leading to the poor car's owner to have a breakdown in the middle of the city. That cat event, the team here at Eurogamer has worked out, is an early game trigger - it seems stealing random cars early in the game will increase the chance of this encounter occurring. Rockstar's guiding hand is more visible here, then, in trying to teach you a lesson: don't steal cars. You're given your own - Jason's two-door coupé utility, a Vapid Creado - that I actually formed quite an emotional bond with in the opening 10-or-so hours of the game. 'Look after this car,' Rockstar insists, tutorialising you how to repair it, customise it, make it all pretty so it's in good condition when you go pick up Lucia for the first time. Shortly after the 10 hour marker, narrative events whisk you away elsewhere and you're given a 'slim jim', a long, thin tool that allows you to break into locked cars - something you could only do with a quick elbow jab before. The benefit here is two-fold; you can break into cars without setting off their alarms, and without breaking glass and lowering their resale value (something quite important in the earlier sections of the game). So, it takes you until Chapter 2 to start being able to more reliably and consistently break into vehicles. Good. And it'll take even longer to break into keyless vehicles. We're in 2026 after all, and it's heavily implied this is when GTA 6 is also set - it stands to reason that many cars run keyless fobs, and your old-school tools won't cut it if you want to break into a Zorruso, rather than an old Vapid truck. But then, even when you're well-armed and ready to start an illustrious new career as Vice City's most nefarious car thief, there's more to consider. Most modern cars also come with trackers: standard trackers simply prevent you modding cars you don't own (not an issue you'll face very often), but advanced trackers are more problematic. Boosting a car with an advanced tracker immediately alerts the cops to your location, and they close in on you fast . The only answer to this problem is flooring it, and outspeeding the signal ping the tracker is sending out: you need to drive fast and cleanly in order to stay mobile long enough for the tracker to deactivate, and this often incurs damage that makes selling these cars to fences a less viable option. You can't even sell cars with trackers installed at all to some fences until you're much, much further into the game. So, long story short, stealing cars is a faff in GTA 6. But I like that. I like that Rockstar has evolved the gameplay formula to more accurately reflect the state of the world in 2026. Modern problems require modern answers, and given that Rockstar has gone above and beyond in its creation of a sandbox simulation of Florida , I feel the immersion would be broken by just being able to saunter up to any car you want and break into it. No, needing a 'slim jim' or a key cloner - or needing to case my victims properly before trying to jack them - makes for a better game as far as I'm concerned. It makes me roleplay Jason and Lucia better, it makes me engage with the game's systems more, it makes me appreciate the cars that I do have whilst I have them. It also improves the flow of the game and how I interact with missions. I recently played GTA: Vice City , and after most missions were wrapped up, I would simply fling the nearest motorist onto the sidewalk, hop in their car, and drive away into the Malibu-styled sunset. I can't simply do that in GTA 6: I need to think about my getaway options, whether there's heat on my car, and where my next best (and cheapest) ride is going to be if a robbery or raid goes awry. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6′s Yard Sales Are Home To Some Amazing Cheap Finds
sources.text: Look, I don’t know much about fashion. I walk around most days in brightly colored cordoroy overalls or long skirts and sweaters. But I know enough to know that Jason Duval has absolutely none of what I think people refer to as “drip.” Guy can’t dress. At the start of the game, his closet is depresso mcspresso. Cargo shorts, some faded jeans, the crappiest old T-shirts you’ve ever seen, a couple of okay Hawaiian shirts, and a single plaid flannel that I assume he wears for “special occasions,” like picking up his girlfriend from jail. Awful. I really love dressing up characters in games and had seen some of the sick outfits you can eventually put Jason and Lucia in later on, so I made it one of my early goals to get the boy something decent to wear. Unfortunately, unless you can rack up a lot of cash and venture pretty far afield, you won’t find too many fashion gems in the early game. The Keys are mostly full of souvenir shops with godawful tourist junk, plasticky sunglasses and ugly shirts and stupid hats. I did find this one pretty sick Vice City tank top and hat in one place, but otherwise the offerings were pretty barren without spending money I didn’t have and desperately needed. Fortunately, I discovered another option: yard sales. My favorite thing about GTA VI ‘s yard sales is probably finding them in the first place. I’ve complained elsewhere about how small and unreadable Leonida’s road signage is, so trying to spot a tiny “Yard Sale” sign with an arrow is a challenge in and of itself. You can see them on main roads, often on medians, stuck underneath other, more important road signs. When you do find these signs, you have to follow them, but Leonida’s roadways aren’t always clear. I once ended up in a back lot with a bunch of really angry assholes while trying to find a yard sale, and another time I drove into an empty field. Hot tip: yard sales are usually in neighborhoods with yards. Once you do find the yard sale, you should buy everything there, every time. I always do. For one, it’s all dirt cheap. Single digit numbers of dollars a lot of the time. And it’s all usually cool, and sometimes rare and unique. An easy-to-find early yard sale in Jason’s own neighborhood had one of the sickest T-shirts I’ve ever seen for sale, and also let me pet an alligator that was wearing a cowboy hat. Speaking of cowboy hats, I followed signs in Gellhorn in Chapter 2 to a different yard sale, where I bought a cowboy hat that I’m told is Arthur Morgan’s and a Hawaiian shirt with cows on it. Later, a guy who was chasing his cow through a field complimented me on my cow shirt, saying he had one just like it. I then went on a crime spree wearing it. Now I’m the Cow Shirt Bandit. I’m unstoppable. — Rebekah Valentine (@duckvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-11-23T04:58:22.293Z — Rebekah Valentine (@duckvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-11-23T04:58:22.293Z I know Jason and Lucia have their sights set on Vice City, which is a ritzier part of Leonida that will almost certainly have fewer yard sales. So while I’m out in the poorer counties, I’m going to enjoy the thrill of yard sale-ing for as long as I can. Outfits like these are sure to make me a huge hit at all the big yacht parties to come. sources.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker who was hospitalized in 2023 has been released on parole with a warning not to do it again
sources.text: Following his guilty plea, Arion Kurtaj was given a seven-year sentence but released "on license" with a warning and restrictions to his online activity.. A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again. Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord. "Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated. "Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from." Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room , using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone. A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence , but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges . That struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again." sources.text: The GTA 6 Cool Dog will help you out of the ocean, and has a big cash bonus for you as well The GTA 6 Jet Ski Dog is one of the many crazy characters that Rockstar have packed into Leonida, and if you're left stranded out at sea then he'll come to your aid. Officially named Cool Dog in the game, if he picks you up then you'll be taken for a ride back to his doggy home on one of the idyllic GTA 6 beaches, when you can not only play with his canine pals but there's also a solid amount of cash waiting for you. To find out more, this is how to meet the Jet Ski Dog in GTA 6. Players have reported finding the GTA 6 Jet Ski Dog at various locations, but the key factor seems to be floating out to sea away from the coast and other boats. I went to the area above in Leonida Bay, and as soon as I started swimming away from my boat I could hear Cool Dog approaching. If they don't appear immediately, swim a bit further away and wait, as it can take several minutes before they arrive. Initially you'll hear barking, followed by music when they get close and pull up. You can hold L2/LT to have a 'conversation' with Cool Dog, but you won't get much of a response. Hit Triangle/Y to climb on Jet Ski Dog's ride, and you'll be whisked away to his home. When the GTA 6 Jet Ski Dog drops you off at his home, you'll also meet lots of his dog friends. You'll be brought a Mini Football you can throw to play fetch, and there are also Wheee Discs and other items to do the same with the various dogs in the area. After some play time with the canines, Cool Dog will disturb the branches at the end of the boat, revealing a wallet on the sand. Grab it, as it contains over $1,200 to give your cash balance a nice little boost! Also have a look around the boat for a metal strongbox in the sand, which contains some cool sunglasses to take away with you. Want to know what to do with that cash? sources.text: Every Missing Person Location and How to Find Them Wondering how to find the Missing Persons in GTA 6? This guide shows you exactly where to find each body, and it explains how the quest plays out depending on your choices. We’ll also explain when you can start the mission, and how to decipher the clues to solve the mystery. Need even more GTA 6 guides? Then check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. The GTA 6 Missing Persons investigation becomes available during Chapter 2, once Lucia has been unlocked and both protagonists are available. To begin the quest, you’ll need to visit the Starlet Motel in Port Gellhorn. This is your safehouse in Chapter 2. Although examining the poster gives you the phone number, calling it won’t immediately reveal the location of the missing tourists. Instead, you’ll need to investigate an abandoned warehouse near Moses’s garage to discover the first clues. The abandoned warehouse is located directly across the road from Moses’s garage in Port Gellhorn. When you arrive, you’ll notice that the main shutter entrance is closed. You can open it with a Slim Jim, or, alternatively you can go to the side of the building and crawl through the small gap in the wall. Once inside, you’ll instantly realise you’re in the lair of a serial killer. You now need to find his trophy room. You’ll eventually reach a disturbing room containing lockers, photographs and newspaper clippings connected to the missing tourists. These images provide the clues needed to find the missing people. Use your in-game phone to photograph all three sets of evidence. The images will be saved in your Gallery under the Creepy Photos album. You’ll take these automatically, and they’ll sync to both Jason and Lucia’s phone. These photos are what we’re going to use to find the bodies. The bodies can be discovered in any order, so you don’t have to follow a particular sequence. There are three missing person locations to discover during the serial killer investigation. Each of them has photograph associated with them that point to where the bodies are buried. After finding each body, interact with it and select the Report Body option. Your character will contact the Kelly County Tip Line to report the discovery. The first missing person can be found inside a pink car at a junkyard in Port Gellhorn. This is arguably the easiest body to locate because the junkyard is close to the Pay ‘n’ Spray. Your character will automatically contact the Kelly County Tip Line to report the discovery. Once the call finishes, you can move on to the next missing person. The second missing person is hidden underneath the floorboards of an abandoned trailer in northern Port Gellhorn. The easiest way to find this location is to look for the large, rusted water tower overlooking the northern part of town. After reporting the discovery, you’ll receive another phone interaction connected to the investigation. The third missing person is the hardest to locate because the photograph only shows a damaged tree beside a body of water. There are several trees in this area that look like the correct one. The picture also looks like it could referring to the air field across the water,Â but the body is actually found in this swamp. You’ll need to travel west of Port Gellhorn towards Wild Hog Point and search the surrounding marshland. The car is difficult to spot because much of it is underwater. There’s a dry patch of land just before it. I reccomend doing this during the day for the best results. Be careful when searching the surrounding water, as alligators can be found in this area. Once you’ve reported the third body, you’ll have completed the main part of the Missing Persons investigation. After reporting all three missing people, you’ll eventually receive another call from the Kelly County Tip Line. The person on the other end will ask you to return to the abandoned warehouse near Moses’s garage. This is where you’ll discover the identity of the serial killer, if you haven’t guessed it already from his voice. After all that effort, the person responsible for operating the tip line is Alvan West, who has been following your investigation. Return to the warehouse and enter through the same hidden opening on its right-hand side. Once inside, make your way back to the Kill Room and speak to Alvan. He’ll explain that he has discovered evidence connected to another missing victim and ask you to investigate an additional locker. However, the photograph inside reveals something much more disturbing: an image of Jason and Lucia. Alvan then attacks, triggering the final part of the hidden investigation. When returning to the warehouse, you have two possible approaches. You can investigate with Jason or Lucia alone, or bring your partner along. Your decision affects how the final encounter plays out and which rewards you can obtain. Here’s what happens with each choice. If you visit Alvan West alone, he’ll attack your character after revealing the photograph of Jason and Lucia. He uses a drug to incapacitate you before taking you to an abandoned mine. You’ll then automatically switch to the other protagonist, who must track down the location and rescue their partner.This route leads to a longer final encounter involving exploration, combat and a confrontation with Alvan. Doing it this way also gives Jason or Lucia the opportunity to collect additional weapons hidden throughout the mine. You can return to the mine after the mission. Alternatively, you can visit Alvan West with both Jason and Lucia. This changes how the encounter plays out. When Alvan attempts to attack your character, your partner intervenes and kills him before the mission can continue into the abandoned mine sequence. This is the quicker way to finish the investigation, although it means missing out

sources.title: How to Get a Key Cloner in GTA 6—Stealing Expensive Cars, Explained
sources.text: If you’re playing GTA 6 and you’ve found an expensive car you want to steal that’s protected with higher-level security features, you might be out of luck. Things like advanced trackers and electronic key controls are tricky, and they can genuinely prevent you from wanting to steal a high-end car, which is basically how they work in real life . Fortunately, you won’t have to wait too long to get your hands on a Key Cloner tool that allows you to gain access to GTA 6’s most valuable cars without triggering their alarms. Their advanced trackers are a different thing entirely, but eventually, you’ll meet someone who can help you with those, too. Here’s how you get a Key Cloner in GTA 6. You don’t find a Key Cloner in GTA 6, but instead, you’re given one halfway through the game’s third chapter by a man called Randy Kozlov. He’s a purveyor of fine motor cars, and he has a list that he wants you to procure for him and his paying customers. Fortunately, Randy wants you to have success in finding and stealing these cars, so he helps you out. When you’re sent out on the mission ‘Clonin’ Keys, Makin’ Gs’, you’ll find that when you get to the car you need to steal (which is gorgeous), Randy will contact you and offer you a Key Cloner that installs on your phone. It’s like the plugin that Cal gives you earlier in the game to track police chatter. It’s a passive thing that lets you do what you need to do with very little effort. It’s also super easy to use. But until you meet Randy and start these missions, you simply cannot find a Key Cloner anywhere. That’s the long and short of it, really. It’s worth stressing that, if a car has the need for a Key Cloner, it will almost certainly have an advanced tracker. These pesky devices will automatically summon police if you drive too slowly , but fortunately, they too can kind of be defeated. To get rid of advanced trackers entirely, you’ll need to progress far into Randy’s wishlist and through the main story. You’ll need to get halfway through Chapter 4, which means putting in a fair wedge of hours. When you pass the ‘Shoot a Promo’ mission in Chapter 4, Randy will summon you to collect a Mamba GT, which spawns in a very specific location. This will come after you’ve stolen ten cars for him and his list. Once you’ve done all of that, Randy will call you to tell you that Pay’n’Spray stations can now remove advanced trackers. The only issue is, you’ll need to get to the Pay’n’Spray without triggering a police response, so it’s not a perfect solution. sources.text: All the endings (and a couple variations) for GTA 6 we've seen so far. Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings! There are multiple endings to GTA 6 , and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed. The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission , but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether. There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future. In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it. A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender." Jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children. Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending. Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it. Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider. Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children. Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand. If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody. After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner. After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together. On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen. How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube ): Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each. Note : You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles. There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet. We'll update this guide if the community finds more endings. sources.text: A YouTuber has uncovered the wildest GTA 6 Easter egg yet. Following a series of arcane clues and pulling a set of switches in the correct order sees players transported back to the 1980s. The Easter egg begins in the R&D tower in Key Lento, GTA 6’s starting area, but spans almost the entire map. Players have to pull a series of switches and press certain buttons to trigger a portal into the past, complete with new voice acting from Danny Dyer as Kent Paul. After scaling the tower, the YouTuber ( Memeio ) noticed that a sound effect from GTA Vice City plays when he messed with the lever and button. A poster for LPL (Leonida Power and Light) in the room then guided him around Leonida to the LPL power substations dotted around the map. Each substation contained letters written on its walls. Memeio was so committed to figuring out the mystery that he actually followed the power cables across the map to track them all down. After putting all the letters together from all 12 substations, Memeio realized they spelled out an interesting phrase: “Life is passing me by.” That phrase was a cheat code in Vice City that sped up the in-game clock. On PlayStation, the code for that cheat was: Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle. Memeio realized that he had to enter that code using all the buttons and switches at the various substations, applying a button to different lever flips and button presses. After pressing the buttons in order, without fast travelling, Memeio got an in-game text to head to Reactor 2 between 7pm and 6am. When he did, a portal opened. Stepping through the portal transported him to Vice City’s Malibu Club, complete with polygonal graphics. Upstairs, he even saw Kent Paul, voiced by British actor Danny Dyer, reprising his role. Danny Dyer is included in the credits for GTA 6 under the “local population" category. For all that effort, you get access to Tommy Vercetti’s iconic floral shirt and his classic Malibu bike, complete with star decals. As requested, here is the entire cutscene! sources.text: Easter Egg Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 Mario You are likely aware that Rockstar’s recently released Grand Theft Auto 6 is a big game. But what you might not understand is just how much of this massive open world is filled with secrets, Easter eggs, and other oddities just waiting to be discovered. This includes a well-hidden block that you can break to reveal two hats that look a lot like what Mario and Luigi might wear. As discovered and shared by Twitter user xGarbett, if you head to Lummox County, the region of GTA 6 located north of Vice City, and start exploring the woods in the southwest portion of Moreau, you’ll be able to find the dilapidated brick and stone ruins of a long-destroyed building. Explore these ruins, and near the top of them is a partially invisible block floating in the air above one of the tallest bits of the out-of-the-way ruin. Jump into that block, just like a famous plumber might do in a Nintendo game, and out will pop two hats for Jason and Lucia. XGarbett shows the precise location in the video below: Head to this location in GTA 6 to unlock a secret Super Mario Easter Egg. Breaking the block like Mario will drop Mario & Luigi style hats for Jason & Lucia. pic.twitter.com/H2CJmdpNod I went there on my own to see if this was all accurate, and yes, I can confirm that this works. I didn’t see the box at first, but after I got up there just like xGarbett did, the hidden cube became visible. However, try as I might, I could not get Jason to break the block by jumping into it. Anyway, I grabbed both, called Lucia, and headed to a clothing shop where we got dressed up in the sunlight with our new, legally distinct hats. sources.title: God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series
sources.text: After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series. Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey. Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir. Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course. There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back. Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon." While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back , too. "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

sources.text: GTA 6 é bom? Confira a review do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI Apenas alguns dias após a grande estreia, GTA 6 já recebeu uma nova atualização no PS5 e Xbox Series X|S que corrige problemas no sistema de salvamento automático — além de outros erros relatados pelos jogadores. O patch, que já está disponível para download, tem cerca de 603 MB e leva o jogo para a versão 01.002.002. Entre as mudanças, a Rockstar também corrigiu falhas que impediam a perda do nível de procurado e o acionamento correto de algumas ligações telefônicas. A atualização ainda resolve problemas de travamento e outros erros que afetavam diferentes atividades do jogo. Desde o lançamento de GTA 6 , os jogadores têm relatado dificuldades com o sistema de salvamento automático. Em alguns casos, os problemas teriam resultado até na perda de dados, fazendo com que parte do progresso nas primeiras horas de jogo desaparecesse. Embora o título salve automaticamente após missões principais e algumas atividades secundárias, o recurso aparentemente não estava funcionando de maneira consistente. Inclusive, houve relatos de jogadores que concluíram missões importantes, mas não tiveram o progresso registrado corretamente. A Rockstar afirma que corrigiu o problema na atualização mais recente, que também resolve outras falhas relacionadas à progressão. Entre elas, estavam erros que impediam o acionamento de ligações importantes para avançar na história ou desbloquear conteúdos de missões. Além de instalar o patch, vale conferir se o salvamento automático está funcionando normalmente. Por precaução, também é recomendável pausar o jogo e salvar o progresso manualmente sempre que possível. Confira as notas completas da atualização: Embora tenha sofrido review bomb da comunidade recentemente, GTA 6 é sem sombra de dúvidas o maior jogo de todos os tempos — não apenas pela sua escala monumental, mas também pelo impacto cultural que vem causando desde seu período de pré-lançamento. Mesmo gigante de diferentes formas possíveis, o game tem uma reprodução bastante assertiva nos consoles . Para aqueles que desejam a cobiçada platina do jogo, saibam que GTA 6 possui uma lista com mais de 50 troféus/conquistas para desbloquear . Além de um mapa interativo que pode te ajudar muito na jogatina, o título também conta com uma série de cheats e trapaças — mas que são ativáveis de forma diferente em comparação aos games anteriores da franquia. E você, já está jogando GTA 6 ? Conte nas redes sociais do VOXL se também enfrentou problemas com o salvamento automático do jogo! sources.text: One GTA 6 actor has no idea who he plays and has asked for fans to help him find his character in the game. Guy A. Fortt, who has previously played a guard in Jessica Jones and The Sopranos, did some performance capture work on GTA 6, but the secrecy of the project meant he didn’t have much context for his scenes. Actors are often kept in the dark when playing a part in Rockstar games. When Roger Clark auditioned for Red Dead Redemption 2 , for example, the only clue he had at the time was he was told to wear cowboy boots. That secrecy, combined with the time between performance and the game’s release, hasn’t helped in Fortt’s case. “So, I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don’t know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in a video that went viral on Instagram . “I auditioned about four or five years ago, they put the balls all over my body and face … and then I forgot all about it.” “Then I get a random email telling me that I’m in GTA 6. This is where I need your help.” Fortt, who is 63 years old and doesn't have a PS5 or play video games himself, is looking for help tracking the character down. According to the actor, his performance saw him standing behind a counter of some kind, and he interacted with Jason and Lucia at one point. He could be some kind of store clerk, a receptionist, or even a cop at a desk, judging by his description. It would be very funny if he ended up being a guard again, like in Jessica Jones and The Sopranos. The community is currently on the hunt for his character, but it might take a while. Rockstar put lots of work into making GTA 6 NPCs varied , hiring dozens and dozens of actors to breathe life into the citizens of Leonida. In a follow-up social media post on day two of the hunt, Fortt said 3 million people were looking for his character in the game, but no luck yet. I assume that's based on social media impressions to his various posts on this, rather than people actively looking for his character in the game. sources.title: Steve Rogers returns to action in final Avengers: Doomsday trailer
sources.text: A new look at Avengers: Doomsday has dropped A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has been released, and it's our best look yet at the upcoming Marvel movie . The new teaser features Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom as he faces the Avengers, but firstly focuses on Steve Rogers' choice of a lifetime as he is visited by the Fantastic Four and leaves Peggy and their son behind. What follows is largely what has been in marketing to date, including the Sentinels being raised by Doom at the X-Mansion. But we get an extra cherry on top: Doomsday's own 'assembling' scene, featuring the X-Men, Captain America, Steve Rogers, and plenty more heroes besides. As one of the OG Avengers, Thor also does his level best to rally the troops, even throwing in a line that might resonate with casual audiences. "I don't even know who half of you are," he says at one point, but is still ready to team up with them against the universe-ending threat of Doom and the incursions. As the official synopsis teases, the heroes from three different universes will have to come together to face their biggest foe yet: Victor Von Doom. The Avengers, Wakandans, and New Avengers join with the Fantastic Four and the original X-Men, meaning the cast list features everyone from Chris Evans to Ian McKellen as more than 30 heroes line up on the battlefield. The new trailer comes after a week of big news for Doomsday. First of all, the VisionQuest finale revealed that Wanda Maximoff is returning for the big team-up movie after she was resurrected by the villain in a post-credits scene. Not only that, but Kevin Feige also debunked a pretty huge theory in a new interview with Empire magazine. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He's Victor Von Doom," Feige teased . sources.title: Avengers: Doomsday’s Final Trailer Shows Steve Rogers’ Family Life Upended By The Fantastic Four
sources.text: Avengers: Doomsday is just under a month away, and we now have the final trailer. It focuses on Steve Rogers’ contrived return as he’s dragged into superhero-ing again after retiring at the end of Avengers: Endgame . The trailer opens by showing us the family life that Steve and his boo Peggy Carter have created, with the two having had a son who’s apparently grown up not knowing about his father’s superhero days. However, things get complicated when the Fantastic Four show up. We also see a fair bit of the New Avengers and the X-Men, including a nod to Cyclops’ iconic “To me, my X-Men!” line, in which James Marsden calls the heroes in for a reprise of the original Avengers spin shot from the 2012 movie. The final trailer can’t help but draw attention to the fact that half of these characters don’t even know each other due to the messiness of Marvel’s attempts to retcon theÂ DoomsdayÂ storyline into old movies after it pivoted away from Kang as the franchise’s next big bad following domestic violence allegations made against actor Jonathan Majors in 2023 . We are but weeks away fromÂ Avengers: Doomsday ‘s premiere on December 18, and Marvel is officially out of time to make this giant ensemble film work, thoughÂ VisionQuest ‘s post-credits scene did at least give a lot of lapsed fans a reason to give a shit again . sources.title: Avengers: Doomsday final trailer has convinced me Steve Rogers got the bad ending in Endgame
sources.text: This is what it's like when worlds collide The Avengers: Doomsday final trailer is here, and it's all about Steve Rogers – from his personal sacrifice of leaving behind Peggy and their son, through to joining Thor and the OG X-Men in a battle against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. But the first minute or so of the trailer is riddled with inconsistencies about the one-time Captain America – and I think it's telling us more than it's letting on. The opening seconds of the Doomsday trailer again shows the moment Steve and Peggy reunite in Endgame. Then, it has a montage of a clean-shaven Steve packing away his Captain America gear, holding his baby boy, and later teaching him how to ride a bike. But the Steve we have seen so far – both in this trailer and elsewhere – shows him with longer hair and a beard, even right up to when the Fantastic Four rock up outside his doorstep. Apart from telling us that Doomsday picks up with Steve and Peggy having a teenage son sometime in the early 1960s, it appears that the Fantastic Four aren't crossing the multiverse to meet him. Instead, my theory is that Steve actually ended up visiting Peggy on Fantastic Four's Earth-828, a decision that caused much of the multiverse to collapse upon itself – and put Steve in Doom's sights. "We didn't know those choices would have consequences," Steve Rogers says of the decision to travel through time in Avengers: Endgame to reclaim the Infinity Stones and use them against Thanos in the Battle for Earth. Simply put, Steve Rogers' past and present actions are catching up to him. He shouldn't have gone back through time (on either occasion), he is potentially on the wrong Earth, and he has a son that should never have existed. So, Avengers: Endgame's final dance could actually be the opening salvo to the universe ending – and caused the incursions (such as the worlds appearing in the sky in one Doomsday trailer moment) that is leading to the collapse of the universe. sources.text: Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18 A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and fans are pretty convinced that Steve Rogers is actually Loki. In the new trailer we see a whole lot of Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter back at their home (though we have no idea what time period or universe they live in)... but the Steve we see outside in the real world walking alongside Thor seems a bit different. "That was a good speech back there," Steve says in the clip. Thor replies, "Yours felt a little average by Cap's standards, don't you think?" Steve then smiles, holds up Mjölnir, and says, "This doesn't bother you, does it?" It would most definitely bother Thor if Loki got to use Mjölnir as a weapon, seeing as only the pure of heart (like Steve Rogers) can hold that hammer, and Loki is far from it. I wasn't sure if I agreed with this one... but then I remembered the previous trailer when Loki shows up at Steve and Peggy's home and says, "I think I can help you." Does this "help" consist of Loki using his shapeshifter powers to become Steve Rogers for the purpose of saving the world from multiple oncoming incursions? This still doesn't explain how Loki is able to leave his post at the center of the universe holding up Yggdrasil... but I'm sure that'll be explained.
